abstract: Which geometric conditions can be imposed on a diffuse grid source at only exponential cost? For every fixed density $0<c<2$ and fixed finite set of directions $D$, we construct conic-centered point classes in the prime square whose independent product law has fractional capacity two on every physical line. Reserving a fixed amount of density permits weighted candidate restriction, alteration of overloaded resources, and a fixed-error application of Kahn's matching theorem. One fixed subset of classes then supports exactly $m=\lfloor cp\rfloor$ points with all $D$-line capacities, with probability $\exp[-O_{c,D}(p)]$ and logarithmic support count $m\log p+O_{c,D}(p)$. The same argument removes every collinear triple containing a pair at infinity-distance at most $\kappa_{c,D}p/\log p$, for some positive constant $\kappa_{c,D}$. We prove a bounded negative pair-interaction form and an exact uniform-grid comparison count for short-pair triples. These positive conditioning results have a precise limitation. An exact Bernoulli embedding and a direct transfer of existing geometric container fingerprints show that the conditioned sources still have typical maximum no-three subsets of size $O(p/(\log p)^{1/4})$. More generally, making a positive linear genuine subset typical requires relative entropy $\Omega(p\sqrt{\log p})$ from the diffuse product law. The obstruction also survives bounded correlations inside independent packets. Complete proofs and small exact controls are supplied. The results identify a high-entropy source and the nonlocal correlation cost left unresolved; they establish neither an all-direction void lower bound nor an unbounded no-three family above $1.8p$.
